## Software requirements

```{r lib, message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#Data containers
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(SingleCellExperiment)

#Data processing
library(CATALYST)
library(scuttle)
library(scater)
library(imcRtools)

#Data visualization
library(cytomapper)
library(dittoSeq)

#Utilities
library(tidyverse)
library(openxlsx)
library(stringr)
```

## Read in single-cell information
based on [SpatialExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SingleCellExperiment.html)
class (Extension of `SingleCellExperiment` class).

### steinbock generated data
The `read_steinbock` function provided by `imcRtools` can now be used to read in
`steinbock` generated data. 

```{r read and inspect steinbock}
spe <- read_steinbock("~/Desktop/IMC processing/steinbock_IMMUCAN/")
spe

#Inspect data
counts(spe[1:5,1:5])
rowData(spe)
colData(spe)
counts(spe[1:5,1:5])
head(spatialCoords(spe)) #main difference between SPE and SCE - single cell location is stored in spatialCoords rather than colData
colPair(spe) #spatial object graphs
```

## Single-cell processing

We can set the `colnames` of the object to generate unique identifiers per cell:

```{r set-colnames}
colnames(spe) <- paste0(spe$sample_id, "_", spe$ObjectNumber)
```

It is also often the case that sample-specific metadata are available externally.
For the current data, we need to link the cancer type (also referred to as "Indication")
to each sample. This metadata is available as external excel file:

```{r add-indication}
meta <- read.xlsx("~/Desktop/IMC processing/steinbock_IMMUCAN/sample_metadata.xlsx")

spe$patient_id <- str_extract_all(spe$sample_id, "[0-9]+", simplify = TRUE)[,2]
spe$indication <- meta$Indication[match(spe$patient_id, meta$Sample.ID)]
```

**Transform counts**

Problem: Right-skewed distribution (bias from highly expressing cells)
Solution: Count transformation using an inverse hyperbolic sine function (arcsinh; common in flow cytometry) = leads to linear-like scale near zero and log-like scale beyond a threshold (`cofactor`)
We apply a `cofactor` of `1`. 

```{r transform-counts, message=FALSE}
#Raw counts
dittoRidgePlot(spe, var = "CD3", group.by = "patient_id", assay = "counts")

#Transformed counts
assay(spe, "exprs") <- asinh(counts(spe)/1)
dittoRidgePlot(spe, var = "CD3", group.by = "patient_id", assay = "exprs")
```
**Define interesting channels**

Subset markers of interest for downstream analysis.

```{r select-features}
rowData(spe)$use_channel <- !grepl("DNA|Histone", rowData(spe)$Clean_Target)
```

## Read in images

Read in multi-channel images (TIFF) and segmentation masks into a
`CytoImageList` container using the `loadImages` function from the `cytomapper` package.

The multi-channel images are saved as 32-bit images while the segmentation masks are
saved as 16-bit images. To correctly scale pixel values of the segmentation
masks when readin them in set `as.is = TRUE`.

```{r read-images}
images <- loadImages("~/Desktop/IMC processing/steinbock_IMMUCAN/img/")
masks <- loadImages("~/Desktop/IMC processing/steinbock_IMMUCAN/masks/", as.is = TRUE)

#set channel-names for multi-channel images
#double-check that the channel order is correct
channelNames(images) <- rownames(spe)
images
```

Add additional metadata to the `elementMetadata` slot of the `CytoImageList` (accessible via mcols)

```{r add-image-metadata}
all.equal(names(images), names(masks))

patient_id <- str_extract_all(names(images), "[0-9]+", simplify = TRUE)[,2]

indication <- meta$Indication[match(patient_id, meta$Sample.ID)] 

mcols(images) <- mcols(masks) <- DataFrame(sample_id = names(images),
                                           patient_id = patient_id,
                                           indication = indication)
```

## Save objects for downstream analysis

```{r save-objects-read-data}
saveRDS(spe, "~/Desktop/IMC processing/data_analysis/spe.rds")
saveRDS(images, "~/Desktop/IMC processing/data_analysis/images.rds")
saveRDS(masks, "~/Desktop/IMC processing/data_analysis/masks.rds")
```
